extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and choosing metal/face type and settings for book printing using specimen sheets that show different typefaces, sizes, faces, leading, and styles in actual body-copy samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface / Foundry identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Named type families and foundries shown as headings (examples on the page: MONOTYPE, CASLON OLD STYLE, SCOTCH ROMAN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimen sheets present the face name prominently so the reader can compare the visual character of different families in set text. Each family heading is followed by body-copy samples in that face to judge overall tone and suitability for book text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point size
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit point sizes are given (examples: SIX POINT, SEVEN POINT, EIGHT POINT, NINE POINT, TEN POINT, ELEVEN POINT, TWELVE POINT, FOURTEEN POINT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each size is shown with the same sample paragraph to evaluate legibility and color (text density) at that size. Use the samples to choose appropriate point size for body text, captions, or display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Face number / cut variant (No. / No. XX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific face/cut identifiers accompany faces (examples: NO. EIGHT, NO. TWENTY-FIVE, NO. THIRTY-SIX, NO. THREE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SEVEN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'No.' designation indicates a particular cut or mold of the face; compare Nos. within and across families to select the precise cut that matches desired weight and proportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solid vs. Leaden setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens are labeled [Solid] or [Leaded] to show text set solid (no added leading) versus with leaded (increased) line spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the same face/size set solid and leaded to judge the effect of leading on readability, page color, and overall appearance; use 'Leaded' where more airy lines or increased readability are desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface style (Roman vs Italic and other stylistic variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stylistic variants are shown (examples: ITALIC NO. TWENTY-FIVE K, Roman faces such as 'SCOTCH ROMAN').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens include both roman and italic settings so designers can evaluate italic behavior (slant, spacing, emphasis) and ensure harmonious pairing in a publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body-copy sample for readability
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard sample paragraph ('When thoughtful Greeks like Polybius saw the fall of Carthage and of Corinth...') is used repeatedly across faces and sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the same paragraph across specimens lets the reader compare legibility, word spacing, hyphenation behavior, and overall text color for practical book-setting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerals and lining figures display
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequences of digits '1234567890' appear throughout the specimens to show numeral design and spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeral samples let the typesetter judge the style and legibility of figures in the chosen face at different sizes, important for tables, running heads, and numbered lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uppercase/display lines and emphatic set-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of all-caps/display lines appear (e.g., 'BUT FAR MORE SERIOUS WAS THE PATENT FACT', 'PEACE THROUGHOUT THE WORLD...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens show how capitals perform in the face—weight, letterspacing, and emphasis—helping decide when to use small caps, full capitals, or other display treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting / body relation notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical casting notes are included (example: 'Ten Point — also cast on Eleven-Point Body', '(12 pt. face)') indicating how a face may be cast or used on a different body size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notes inform the printer about alternate casting options and how a face will appear when cast on a differing body, useful when matching faces or conserving matrices in production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of spacing/line color across sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated presentation of the same text in multiple sizes and leadings illustrates differences in 'color' (text density) and spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare pages (e.g., eight-point vs twelve-point, solid vs leaded) to decide acceptable text color and measure how size and leading affect overall page texture in the final printed book.
